bill.title: Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection relating to "Quality Control Standards for Automated Valuation Models".
bill.latestActionText: Referred to the House Committee on Financial Services.
bill.officialSummary: This joint resolution nullifies the final rule issued by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, the Federal Reserve System, the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, the National Credit Union Administration, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, and the Federal Housing Finance Agency titled Quality Control Standards for Automated Valuation Models and published on August 7, 2024. The rule requires the implementation of quality control standards for automated valuation models used by mortgage originators and secondary market issuers when determining the value of real estate securing a mortgage.

classification.plainSummary: This joint resolution would nullify a federal rule published in August 2024 that requires quality control standards for automated valuation models—computer systems used to estimate property values when issuing or selling mortgages. If enacted, the resolution would eliminate these standards and prevent the rule from taking effect. The rule was issued jointly by six federal financial regulators.

industries.rationale: Mortgage originators and secondary market issuers would no longer face quality control requirements for automated valuation models they use.
Real estate valuation practices for mortgage-secured properties would be directly affected by the removal of automated model standards.
Developers and vendors of automated valuation model software would face different regulatory expectations if the rule is nullified.

plain.whatItDoes: This joint resolution would cancel the final rule issued by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, the Federal Reserve System, the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, the National Credit Union Administration, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, and the Federal Housing Finance Agency titled Quality Control Standards for Automated Valuation Models and published on August 7, 2024.
plain.whoItTouches: Anyone with a bank account, a loan or savings.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in dealing with banks and lenders. Nothing has changed yet. Most bills never become law.
plain.source: Reworded from the official summary. Staff at the Congressional Research Service wrote that summary. It is public domain, and the full text of it is further down this page.

method.formula: score = Σ_industries ( donorShare(industry) × billWeight(industry) ), where billWeight = classifierConfidence / Σ classifierConfidence. Range 0–1, read as a weighted share of disclosed itemized money.

ordinary.text: They wrote this bill. Sponsoring a bill about your own district's industry is the ordinary case, not the odd one.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
